correctness.rationale: A missing-edge pair gives the sharp operator-norm lower bound 1/(m-1), since centered coordinate vectors have norm squared (m-1)/m. The explicit cone kernel then has eigenvalues 1, -1/m, and (m-1)/m times all nonconstant base eigenvalues, proving the upper bound. Averaging any feasible cone kernel over the transitive core automorphism group makes all spokes b<=1/m, and its remaining eigenvalues include (1-b) times the full nonconstant spectrum of a feasible core kernel; this proves the matching lower bound. Complete and disconnected cores are handled. The P4 strict boundary uses an exact 5x5 characteristic polynomial and independent P4 reflection-block bound. The supplied standard-library verifier passed 895 exact rational checks; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The invariant transfers an unknown or known exact convex FMMC solution on any vertex-transitive graph, with possibly many distinct edge orbits, to its universal-vertex cone by a universal factor and explicit new transition matrix; the coefficient is independent of detailed topology. A universal inequality for all bases and a strict P4 boundary isolate precisely why the symmetry hypothesis matters. This is a structural solution reduction across infinitely many nonisomorphic graphs, not merely another calculation of a known wheel instance.
